scope: Consolidated factcheck for all /docs/* pages. Per-page claims grouped under page slug. Source citations reference code, not README (README diverges from code in 2 places — see flags).

claims.claim: First-load requires internet; afterward offline.
Two-button rating: Don't know / Know.
Six card shapes: recognition, recall, listening, writing, kanji reading, grammar.
Four card creation methods: Text, Image, Audio, Anki.
Text mode: tokenize + dictionary lookup + preview.
Image mode: on-device OCR, model downloads on first use.
Audio mode: WAV-only, on-device STT, model downloads on first use.
Anki import: .apkg, auto-detect fields.
Auto-fill furigana, POS, JLPT level; duplicates skipped.

Lesson pulls new cards, due reviews, mixed views.
New cards per day from pace setting; due cards take priority.
Six card shapes: recognition, recall, listening, writing, kanji reading, grammar.

claims.claim: Bilingual dictionaries (Japanese to user language).
Audio from NHK and native-speaker corpora.

claims.claim: Furigana auto-generated for all Japanese text.
Gradual hiding: furigana disappears for learned kanji.
Writing practice = stroke order animation, not handwriting recognition.
Kanji organized by JLPT N5-N1.
Reading tests: word with hidden furigana, supply reading.
Kanji enters collection via vocabulary cards, imported sets, grammar examples.
Grammar reference organized by JLPT N5-N1.
Examples use vocabulary user has learned (contextual examples).
Furigana and translation shown even for unfamiliar vocabulary.
Grammar search by particle or verb form.

claims.claim: Grammar cards: pattern identification, completion, mutation.
Grammar cards rated with two-button system + FSRS.
Phrase corpus from native content (visual novels, anime).
Original voice acting, not synthesized.
N+1 selection driven by known-vocabulary index.
Listening cards: play audio, transcribe or match.
Audio plays at natural speed, no slowdown.
Phrases enter reviews automatically as vocabulary grows.
Phrases are individual sentences, not full episodes.
OCR and STT run on-device; never upload user media.
OCR supports PNG, JPEG, WebP with file size limit.
OCR model downloads on first use, then runs offline.
OCR struggles with stylized fonts, low contrast, vertical layouts, small chars; no handwriting.

iOS is the next platform in active development.
